```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(readr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork);

proj <- here("VoleMUPs")

D <- file.path(cfg$data_root, "derived")
rd <- function(...) read_tsv(file.path(D, ...), show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 10000)
opt <- function(...) if (file.exists(file.path(D, ...))) rd(...) else NULL
figdir <- file.path(D, "summary", "figures"); dir.create(figdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
save_fig <- function(p, name, w, h) ggsave(file.path(figdir, name), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200, bg = "white")

species <- rd("summary", "species.tsv")
genes <- rd("summary", "genes.tsv")
regions <- rd("summary", "regions.tsv")

rgenes <- rd("regions", "region_genes.tsv")
flanks <- rd("regions", "flanks.tsv")
anchors <- rd("regions", "anchors.tsv")
cls <- rd("tree", "classification.tsv")
clades <- opt("tree", "clades.tsv")
expr <- opt("expression", "counts.tsv")
lip <- rd("annotated", "lipocalins.tsv")

grp_cols <- c(Murinae = "#D55E00", Gerbillinae = "#E69F00", Neotominae = "#CC79A7", Cricetinae = "#56B4E9",
              Arvicolinae = "#009E73", `other rodents` = "#8C6D31", `non-rodents` = "#7F7F7F", reference = "#000000")
clade_cols <- c(MUP = "#D55E00", OBP = "#0072B2", OBP2 = "#7B5EA7", other = "#BDBDBD")
lab_of <- setNames(paste0(species$common, " (", species$name, ")"), species$slug)
short_of <- setNames(species$common, species$slug)
short_of[c("microtus_ochrogaster", "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd1", "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd2", "mus_spretus")] <-
  c("prairie vole (MicOch1.0, 2012)", "prairie vole (UC Davis 2026, hap1)", "prairie vole (UC Davis 2026, hap2)",
    "Algerian mouse (control)")
sp_order <- species$slug
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
n_of <- function(slug, cl, intact = NA) {
  x <- genes %>% filter(.data$slug == !!slug, clade == cl)
  if (!is.na(intact)) x <- x %>% filter(intact == !!intact)
  nrow(x)
}
```

## The question

House mice put large amounts of **major urinary proteins (MUPs)** into their urine. MUPs are lipocalins: small
barrel-shaped proteins with a pocket that binds small odour molecules. In mice they carry and slowly release volatile
pheromones, and some act as signals themselves. Darcin (MUP20) is a male protein that makes females attracted to, and
remember, a male's scent (Roberts et al. 2010, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1186/1741-7007-8-75)). The C57BL/6 mouse
genome has 21 *Mup* genes and about as many *Mup* pseudogenes in one cluster on chromosome 4 (Mudge et al. 2008,
[doi](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2008-9-5-r91); Charkoftaki et al. 2019,
[doi](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40246-019-0191-9)).

Most other mammals are different. Logan et al. (2008, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0003280)) found a single
ancestral *Mup* gene in most placental mammals, with separate expansions in mouse, rat, horse and grey mouse lemur. Humans
keep only a pseudogene (*MUPP*). In bank voles (*Myodes glareolus*) the main urinary and salivary lipocalins are not MUPs
but **odorant-binding proteins (OBPs)** similar to hamster aphrodisin (Stopková et al. 2010,
[doi](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-11-45)), and male bank vole urine carries a male-biased OBP-type lipocalin,
glareosin (Loxley et al. 2017, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsob.170135)), which on its own did not explain female
attraction to male scent (Coombes et al. 2024, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-55235-x)). Water vole males
secrete another such lipocalin, arvicolin (Nagnan-Le Meillour et al. 2019,
[doi](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-54935-z)), and the Roborovski hamster's urine has roborovskin (Turton et al.
2010, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1093/chemse/bjq060)).

**Question.** Does the prairie vole (*Microtus ochrogaster*) have MUP genes, and if so how many, are they intact, and
are they switched on in the liver the way mouse MUPs are? Or, like the bank vole, does it rely on OBP-type lipocalins?

## The plain answer

```{r answer, results = "asis"}
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
qv <- if (!is.null(qc)) setNames(qc$value, qc$check) else c()
mm_row <- species %>% filter(slug == "mus_musculus")
pv_mup <- genes %>% filter(slug == "microtus_ochrogaster", clade == "MUP")
pvu_mup <- genes %>% filter(slug == "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd1", clade == "MUP", status != "fragment")
voles <- species %>% filter(group == "Arvicolinae")
vole_closed <- voles %>% filter(MUP_region == "closed")
rpm_of <- function(sl, ids) if (is.null(expr)) NA else sum(expr$rpm[expr$slug == sl & expr$gene_id %in% ids])
mup_ids <- function(sl) sub(".*\\|", "", genes$id[genes$slug == sl & genes$clade == "MUP"])
alb_of <- function(sl) if (is.null(expr)) NA else sum(expr$rpm[expr$slug == sl & expr$symbol == "Alb"])
mm_mup_rpm <- if (is.null(expr)) NA else sum(expr$rpm[expr$slug == "mus_musculus" & (grepl("^Mup", expr$symbol))])
txt <- c(
  sprintf("- **Yes: one MUP gene.** The prairie vole's RefSeq annotation (MicOch1.0, 2012) has %d gene in the MUP clade of the lipocalin tree (%s, named \"major urinary protein 4-like\"), and the 2026 UC Davis long-read assembly has %d intact MUP gene and no other MUP-family locus anywhere in the genome (%s short MUP-like matches, under 40%% of a MUP's length, are not counted). The protein is 69%% identical to mouse MUP4 and 95%% to the meadow vole's MUP, against about 30%% to the OBPs. For comparison, the C57BL/6 mouse annotation names %s *Mup* genes and %s *Mup* pseudogenes.",
          nrow(pv_mup), paste(pv_mup$symbol, collapse = ", "), sum(pvu_mup$intact %in% c(TRUE, "True")),
          qv[["microtus_ochrogaster_ucd1_MUP_fragments_genome"]], qv[["mouse_Mup_genes_annotated"]], qv[["mouse_Mup_pseudogenes_annotated"]]),
  sprintf("- **Every vole has exactly one, in the ancestral place.** In all %d vole genomes in which both sides of the neighbourhood were found, a single MUP gene sits between *Zfp37* and *Slc46a2*, the genes that flank the 2.2 Mb mouse *Mup* cluster; the vole stretch is %s-%s kb long. Hamsters, the deer mouse, the gerbil and the beaver also have one or two there; mouse (%s kb), rat (%s kb), golden hamster and horse have expanded families.",
          nrow(vole_closed), fmt(min(vole_closed$MUP_region_kb)), fmt(max(vole_closed$MUP_region_kb)),
          fmt(mm_row$MUP_region_kb), fmt(species$MUP_region_kb[species$slug == "rattus_norvegicus"])),
  sprintf("- **Voles expanded the OBPs instead.** The 2026 prairie vole assembly has %d intact genes in the X-linked OBP1 / aphrodisin clade (%d more broken or partial), and the RefSeq-annotated voles carry %s-%s intact ones (the low end is the fragmented reed vole assembly); mouse has %d. The 2012 assembly misses most of the prairie vole OBP cluster: that stretch is full of assembly gaps.",
          species$OBP_intact[species$slug == "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd1"], species$OBP_other[species$slug == "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd1"],
          min(voles$OBP_intact[voles$source == "refseq"]), max(voles$OBP_intact[voles$source == "refseq"]),
          species$OBP_intact[species$slug == "mus_musculus"]))
if (!is.null(expr)) txt <- c(txt,
  sprintf("- **On in prairie vole liver, off in meadow and bank vole liver.** In male liver RNA-seq the prairie vole MUP gene gives %s reads per million (RPM; albumin %s RPM). The meadow vole's (same lab and protocol) gives %s RPM and the bank vole's %s RPM. All mouse *Mup* transcripts together give %s RPM in a C57BL/6 male (albumin %s RPM). One animal per species.",
          fmt(rpm_of("microtus_ochrogaster", mup_ids("microtus_ochrogaster"))), fmt(alb_of("microtus_ochrogaster")),
          fmt(rpm_of("microtus_pennsylvanicus", mup_ids("microtus_pennsylvanicus"))),
          fmt(rpm_of("myodes_glareolus", mup_ids("myodes_glareolus"))), fmt(mm_mup_rpm), fmt(alb_of("mus_musculus"))))
cat(paste(txt, collapse = "\n"))
```

## What we searched

```{r species-table}
species %>% transmute(Species = paste0(common, " (*", name, "*)"), Group = group,
                      Source = ifelse(source == "refseq", "RefSeq annotation + region DNA", "whole-genome DNA search"),
                      Accession = accession) %>% kable()
```

Three kinds of evidence were combined (scripts in `scripts/`, steps 01-07):

1. **Gene annotations (Step 02).** NCBI RefSeq has annotated `r sum(species$source == "refseq")` of these genomes. In the
   longest protein of every gene, HMMER `hmmsearch` looked for the Pfam lipocalin domain (PF00061, independent
   E < 10^-3^). Genes named as MUPs, OBPs, aphrodisins or lipocalins were added so that annotated pseudogenes (which have
   no protein) are counted too.
2. **The genome sequence itself (Steps 03-04).** Genes that sit next to each other in the mouse usually stay neighbours in
   other rodents (**synteny**). The 8 protein-coding genes on each side of three mouse lipocalin clusters (the *Mup*
   cluster on chromosome 4; *Obp1a*/*Obp1b* on chromosome X; the chromosome 2 lipocalin cluster holding *Obp2a*/*Obp2b*)
   were found in each genome by name, and the DNA between them was downloaded. miniprot (Li 2023, splice-aware
   protein-to-genome alignment) aligned `r nrow(read_lines(file.path(D, "queries", "queries.faa")) %>% tibble() %>% filter(str_starts(., ">")))` query proteins to that DNA:
   mouse, rat, horse, cat and dog MUPs, mouse and bank vole OBPs, hamster aphrodisin, water vole arvicolin, and every
   other secreted mouse lipocalin as a decoy. A DNA hit is **intact** when it has no frameshift and no premature stop
   and covers at least 80% of its query; **disrupted** when it has either (a possible pseudogene, or an error in the
   assembly); **partial** otherwise. Assembly gaps (runs of 10 or more N) were counted. Genomes without an annotation
   (the 2026 UC Davis prairie vole, field, common and montane voles, the Algerian mouse *Mus spretus* as a positive
   control, the Djungarian hamster) were searched whole, with the flanking genes' proteins added to the queries.
3. **A gene tree (Step 05).** Names like "major urinary protein 4-like" come from a single best BLAST match. To place
   every candidate, the lipocalin domains of all RefSeq candidates (cytosolic fatty-acid-binding proteins removed) were
   aligned with MAFFT, trimmed with trimAl (`-gappyout`) and built into a maximum-likelihood tree with IQ-TREE 3 (LG+G4,
   fast search, SH-aLRT support), rooted on ApoD. The **MUP clade** is the smallest clade holding every mouse MUP, the
   horse, cat and dog MUP allergens, and every lipocalin found in the MUP neighbourhood (between the genes flanking
   the mouse cluster) of any genome. Anchoring on position as well as on the references keeps the clade stable when the
   deep branching order inside it is uncertain (in the focused tree the hamster and vole MUPs branch just outside the
   mouse + horse + carnivore MUPs); the quality checks list every gene in the clade that is not named as a MUP. The
   **OBP clade** (the X-linked OBP1 / aphrodisin family) is the smallest holding
   hamster aphrodisin, the three bank vole OBPs and mouse Obp1a/Obp1b; **OBP2** the smallest holding mouse and human
   OBP2A/OBP2B. DNA hits that are not in a tree take the clade of their best-matching query protein. A focused tree
   (the MUP and OBP clades and everything between them, the OBP2 clade, 20 mouse and human lipocalins from the rest of
   the family, all MUP-family DNA loci and the UC Davis prairie vole's OBP-family loci) was re-estimated with MAFFT
   L-INS-i, ModelFinder (LG, WAG, JTT families) and 1,000 ultrafast bootstraps plus 1,000 SH-aLRT replicates, rooted
   on mouse ApoD.
4. **Liver RNA-seq (Step 06).** The first 120 MB of read-1 FASTQ from male liver of the prairie vole and meadow vole
   (UC Davis genome project, ENA PRJEB108798), a male C57BL/6 mouse (DRR188168, positive control) and a bank vole
   (SRR29282985, sex not given) were matched to each species' lipocalin transcripts (longest RefSeq transcript per
   gene) by 25-letter words shared with no other gene; reads from sequence shared among the near-identical mouse MUPs
   are pooled as "Mup (shared sequence)". Albumin (*Alb*), apolipoprotein A-I (*Apoa1*) and beta-actin (*Actb*) are
   yardsticks.

## Quality checks

```{r qc, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(qc)) kable(qc) else cat("qc.tsv not built yet.\n")
```

```{r qc-flanks}
reg_tab <- regions %>% filter(found) %>% group_by(slug, region) %>%
  summarise(parts = n(), kb = round(sum(length) / 1000, 1), gaps = sum(n_gaps, na.rm = TRUE),
            gap_bp = sum(gap_bp, na.rm = TRUE), open = any(!is.na(open) & open != ""), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(species = short_of[slug]) %>% arrange(match(slug, sp_order))
reg_tab %>% select(species, region, parts, kb, gaps, gap_bp, open) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = c(kb, gaps, open), names_glue = "{region} {.value}") %>%
  kable(caption = "Each region between the flanking genes: length (kb), assembly gaps inside it, and whether it runs off a scaffold end ('open').")
```

## Results

### 1. The lipocalin gene tree

```{r tree, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
tf <- file.path(D, "tree", "focused", "mup_obp.rooted.nwk")
if (file.exists(tf)) {
  tr <- read.tree(tf)
  tipd <- cls %>% filter(tip %in% tr$tip.label) %>%
    left_join(species %>% select(slug, group, common), by = "slug") %>%
    mutate(group = ifelse(slug == "uniprot", "reference", group),
           clade = ifelse(clade == "", "other", clade),
           focal = slug %in% c("microtus_ochrogaster", "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd1", "microtus_ochrogaster_ucd2"),
           tl = case_when(focal & clade == "MUP" ~ paste0("prairie vole MUP (", ifelse(source == "genome", "UC Davis ", ""), symbol, ")"),
                          slug == "uniprot" ~ paste(gsub("_", " ", description), sub("_MUP|_Stopkova2010", "", symbol)),
                          TRUE ~ NA_character_))
  tipd$tl[tipd$slug == "mus_musculus" & tipd$symbol == "Mup20"] <- "mouse Mup20 (darcin)"
  p <- ggtree(tr, layout = "circular", linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey40") %<+% tipd +
    geom_tippoint(aes(colour = group, size = focal)) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.9, `TRUE` = 2.6), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grp_cols, name = NULL) +
    geom_tiplab2(aes(label = tl), size = 2.4, offset = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  for (cl in c("MUP", "OBP", "OBP2")) {
    tt <- tipd$tip[tipd$clade == cl]
    if (length(tt) >= 2) {
      node <- getMRCA(tr, tt)
      p <- p + geom_hilight(node = node, fill = clade_cols[cl], alpha = 0.12) +
        geom_cladelab(node = node, label = cl, offset = 0.4, barcolour = clade_cols[cl], textcolour = clade_cols[cl],
                      fontsize = 3.5)
    }
  }
  save_fig(p, "fig1_tree.png", 10, 10)
  p
}
```

### 2. Counts per species

```{r counts, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.5}
cnt <- genes %>% filter(clade %in% c("MUP", "OBP", "OBP2")) %>%
  mutate(state = ifelse(intact %in% c(TRUE, "True"), "intact / protein-coding", "pseudogene, disrupted or partial")) %>%
  count(slug, clade, state) %>% complete(slug = sp_order, clade, state, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  mutate(species = factor(short_of[slug], levels = rev(short_of[sp_order])))
p <- ggplot(cnt, aes(n, species, fill = clade, alpha = state)) + geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~clade, scales = "free_x", labeller = as_labeller(c(MUP = "MUP clade", OBP = "OBP1 / aphrodisin clade",
                                                                 OBP2 = "OBP2 clade"))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clade_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`intact / protein-coding` = 1, `pseudogene, disrupted or partial` = 0.4), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genes", y = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(p, "fig2_counts.png", 9, 6.5)
p
```

### 3. The MUP neighbourhood

```{r synteny-mup, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7.5}
mrows <- rd("summary", "map_rows.tsv")
mgenes <- rd("summary", "map_genes.tsv")
mgaps <- rd("summary", "map_gaps.tsv")
kind_lab <- c(MUP = "MUP clade", OBP = "OBP clade", OBP2 = "OBP2 clade", lipo = "other lipocalin",
              flank = "flanking gene", gene = "other gene")
draw_region <- function(reg) {
  rr <- mrows %>% filter(region == reg) %>% arrange(match(slug, sp_order), part) %>%
    mutate(row = row_number(), lab = paste0(short_of[slug], ifelse(part > 1, paste0(" (", part, ")"), ""),
                                            "  ", ifelse(end - start >= 1e6, sprintf("%.2f Mb", (end - start) / 1e6),
                                                          paste0(round((end - start) / 1000), " kb"))))
  pos <- function(d) d %>% inner_join(rr %>% select(region_id, row, lo, hi, flip), by = "region_id") %>%
    mutate(x0 = (pmax(start, lo) - lo) / pmax(1, hi - lo), x1 = (pmin(end, hi) - lo) / pmax(1, hi - lo),
           a = ifelse(flip, 1 - x1, x0), b = ifelse(flip, 1 - x0, x1))
  g <- pos(mgenes) %>% mutate(kind = factor(kind_lab[kind], levels = kind_lab),
                              broken = grepl("pseudo|disrupted|partial", status),
                              h = ifelse(kind == "other gene", 0.12, 0.3))
  gp <- pos(mgaps)
  ggplot(g) +
    geom_segment(data = rr, aes(x = 0, xend = 1, y = row, yend = row), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = a, xmax = pmax(b, a + 0.003), ymin = row - h, ymax = row + h, fill = kind, alpha = broken)) +
    geom_rect(data = gp, aes(xmin = a, xmax = pmax(b, a + 0.002), ymin = row + 0.33, ymax = row + 0.45),
              fill = "#D62728") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 0.4), labels = c("intact / annotated protein", "pseudogene or broken hit"),
                       name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`MUP clade` = clade_cols[["MUP"]], `OBP clade` = clade_cols[["OBP"]],
                                 `OBP2 clade` = clade_cols[["OBP2"]], `flanking gene` = "grey35",
                                 `other lipocalin` = "#E7C9A9", `other gene` = "grey75"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = rr$row, labels = rr$lab, expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = expansion(add = 0.01)) +
    labs(x = "Region between the innermost flanking genes, each row scaled to its own length (red: assembly gaps)", y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
}
p <- draw_region("MUP")
save_fig(p, "fig3_synteny_mup.png", 10, 7.5)
p
```

### 5. Is the vole MUP gene switched on in the liver?

```{r expression, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
if (!is.null(expr)) {
  e <- expr %>% left_join(genes %>% transmute(slug, gene_id = sub(".*\\|", "", id), clade), by = c("slug", "gene_id")) %>%
    mutate(clade = ifelse(gene_id == "MUPFAM", "MUP", clade),
           kind = case_when(description == "yardstick" ~ symbol, clade %in% c("MUP", "OBP", "OBP2") ~ paste(clade, "clade"),
                            TRUE ~ "other lipocalins"),
           kind = factor(kind, levels = rev(c("Alb", "Apoa1", "Actb", "MUP clade", "OBP clade", "OBP2 clade", "other lipocalins")))) %>%
    group_by(sample, slug, kind) %>% summarise(rpm = sum(rpm), .groups = "drop")
  p <- ggplot(e, aes(pmax(rpm, 0.5), kind, fill = kind)) + geom_col() + facet_wrap(~sample, ncol = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = comma(round(rpm))), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.8) +
    scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
    labs(x = "Reads per million (log scale)", y = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`MUP clade` = clade_cols[["MUP"]], `OBP clade` = clade_cols[["OBP"]],
                                 `OBP2 clade` = clade_cols[["OBP2"]], `other lipocalins` = "grey60", Alb = "grey30",
                                 Apoa1 = "grey30", Actb = "grey30"), guide = "none")
  save_fig(p, "fig5_liver.png", 9, 5)
  p
}
```

The table shows the single genes behind the MUP bars: in voles there is only one MUP gene; in the mouse, reads that
fall in sequence shared by several near-identical MUPs are pooled as "Mup (shared sequence)".

```{r expression-table}
if (!is.null(expr)) {
  mup_e <- expr %>% left_join(genes %>% transmute(slug, gene_id = sub(".*\\|", "", id), clade), by = c("slug", "gene_id")) %>%
    filter(clade == "MUP" | gene_id == "MUPFAM") %>% group_by(sample) %>%
    summarise(genes = n(), reads = sum(reads), reads_total = first(reads_total), rpm = sum(rpm),
              top = paste(head(paste0(symbol, " ", comma(round(rpm))), 4), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
  alb <- expr %>% filter(symbol == "Alb") %>% select(sample, alb_rpm = rpm)
  kable(mup_e %>% left_join(alb, by = "sample") %>% mutate(`MUP / albumin` = sprintf("%.3f", rpm / alb_rpm)),
        caption = "MUP-clade reads in each liver sample (RPM = reads per million sampled reads).")
}
xc <- opt("expression", "vole_mup_crosscheck.tsv")
if (!is.null(xc)) kable(xc %>% select(sample, reads_total, reads_any_vole_mup, rpm),
                        caption = "Cross-check that does not depend on each species' gene model: reads matching any of the three vole MUP transcripts (prairie, meadow, bank vole; 21-letter words).")
```

## Caveats

- **Annotation-named genes are a start, not proof.** The tree, not the name, decides what counts as a MUP. Clades in the
  full family tree come from a fast search; their support values are in the table above.
- **A gap is not an absence.** MicOch1.0 (2012) is a short-read assembly in many small contigs. Assembly gaps inside a
  region are counted above, and the 2026 UC Davis long-read assembly is searched independently.
- **Disrupted is not always a pseudogene.** Frameshifts and stops in DNA hits can be sequencing errors, especially in
  short-read assemblies, or splice junctions miniprot could not model (all OBP2-type hits in the UC Davis assembly carry
  one frameshift, while RefSeq models the same genes as intact in MicOch1.0). OBP counts from DNA hits are rough.
- **Which protein.** The prairie vole MUP gene has several RefSeq models: a 188-aa form with the usual MUP signal
  peptide and C-terminus (isoform X2), and longer ones with an extra start or another last exon (up to 231 aa). The
  pipeline keeps the longest model per gene; the tree uses only the lipocalin domain, which all forms share. Which form
  the liver makes was not checked.
- **The second UC Davis haplotype has no X chromosome.** The sequenced vole was male, and hap2 holds only the
  autosomes, so the X-linked OBP1 cluster cannot be in it; its OBP1 count is not a real zero.
- **Positive control.** The whole-genome search finds a MUP cluster in *Mus spretus* (an unannotated mouse genome) and
  recovers the mouse cluster from its DNA, so a cluster in a vole would not have been missed. It does not prove that
  every member of a large cluster is counted: near-identical copies can collapse in an assembly.
- **Expression from one liver per species, first reads only.** The RNA-seq check uses one male per species and the first
  1-3 million reads of each file. It can show whether a gene makes up a large share of liver mRNA (as mouse MUPs do),
  not small differences. Kidney, salivary and preputial glands were not checked.
- **Genome, not urine.** This says which genes voles have and whether the liver makes one of them; it does not show
  which proteins are in prairie vole urine. Urine proteomics would.
